questions.question: A warehouse system accepts an unauthorized change to a stock record. Which security property is directly compromised?

options.a: Availability

questions.explanation: Integrity protects records against unauthorized alteration.

questions.question: A user has proved their identity and wants to export a private report. Which control decides if the export is allowed?

options.a: Compression

questions.explanation: Authorization decides what an authenticated caller is allowed to do.

questions.question: Which technique is appropriate for storing passwords for verification?

options.a: A salted Argon2id password hash
options.c: A shared encrypted file with the key beside it

questions.explanation: A dedicated password hash and unique salt raise the cost of offline guessing.

questions.question: A web form's username is used in a SQL query. Which change prevents the value from becoming SQL syntax?

options.a: Remove whitespace from usernames
options.c: Bind the username as a query parameter
options.d: Hide errors from the UI alone

questions.explanation: Parameter binding separates SQL instructions from user-provided values.

questions.question: A support role should read assigned tickets. Which permissions follow least privilege? Select all that apply.

options.a: Read ticket rows assigned to that role
options.c: See only ticket fields needed for the job

questions.explanation: Least privilege limits both row access and the data fields the role needs.

questions.question: A stored profile bio injects JavaScript into the page whenever another user views it. What is the attack called?

options.a: Stored cross-site scripting

questions.explanation: Stored XSS persists malicious input and later executes it in visitors' browsers.

questions.question: A cookie-authenticated app checks a secret tied to the current session on every state-changing form submission. What is the secret used for?

options.a: Content compression

questions.explanation: A session-bound CSRF token lets the server verify that a form request includes a value a foreign origin should not know.

questions.question: A signed-in caller changes the invoice ID in a URL and receives another customer's invoice. What server check is missing?

options.a: Whether the ID is a positive integer
options.b: Whether the caller can read that specific invoice
options.d: Whether the invoice uses the newest format

questions.explanation: Object-level authorization checks the caller's access to the requested resource.

questions.question: Which cookie flag blocks access to the cookie through document.cookie?

options.a: Domain

questions.explanation: HttpOnly marks the cookie as inaccessible to JavaScript through ordinary browser cookie APIs.

questions.question: A server downloads files from a small set of approved external hosts. Which measures help prevent server-side request forgery? Select all that apply.

options.a: Validate destinations against an explicit allowlist
options.b: Trust a URL if its displayed text contains 'https'
options.c: Disable redirects or validate each new destination
options.d: Return all fetched bytes before validating the URL

questions.explanation: Destination validation and redirect handling constrain which servers can be reached.

questions.question: What does a normal TLS hostname check verify?

options.a: That the server certificate covers the hostname the client requested
options.b: That every HTTP response contains JSON
options.c: That the user has permission to edit the server
options.d: That the server stores encrypted backups

questions.explanation: Hostname verification binds the certificate identity to the server name being contacted.

questions.question: A public repository exposed a live credential. Which action makes that credential unusable?

options.a: Delete the local git branch only
options.c: Revoke the credential at its issuer
options.d: Rename the variable that holds it

questions.explanation: Revocation invalidates copies of the exposed credential, including copies outside the repository.

questions.question: An attacker signs in with username and password pairs leaked by a different service. What is this attack called?

options.a: Password spraying with one guessed password

questions.explanation: Credential stuffing reuses previously leaked credential pairs across services.

questions.question: What does verifying a release signature with a trusted public key establish?

options.a: That the package has no bugs
options.b: That the package runs on every system
options.d: That the signed content verifies against the trusted key

questions.explanation: A matching signature establishes integrity and links the signed content to possession of the signing key.

questions.question: Which practices help prevent user uploads from executing as application code? Select all that apply.

options.a: Keep upload storage outside executable application directories
options.b: Treat uploaded scripts as server templates
options.c: Serve uploads as data through a controlled download handler
options.d: Choose executability based only on the file's name

questions.explanation: Separating uploads from executable code and streaming them as data avoids invoking interpreters.

questions.question: Which log entry supports a sign-in investigation while minimizing credential exposure?

options.a: Outcome, timestamp, and account ID

questions.explanation: Outcomes and account IDs can support investigation without logging secrets.

questions.question: Which construction authenticates a message with a shared secret key?

options.a: CRC32

questions.explanation: HMAC combines a secret key with a hash function to produce a message authentication code.

questions.question: If an attacker copies the backup storage, which practice helps protect backup contents?

options.a: Store all backup files next to a plaintext copy of their key
options.b: Encrypt the backups and protect the keys separately

questions.explanation: Backup encryption protects confidentiality when keys are kept separate from copied data.

questions.question: What does a software bill of materials help a team identify during a dependency incident?

options.a: The list of currently signed-in users
options.b: The time a feature flag was created
options.d: The components and versions shipped in an artifact

questions.explanation: An SBOM inventories dependencies and versions that can be checked for exposure.

questions.question: After deploying a vulnerability fix, which checks help verify that the original exposure is closed? Select all that apply.

options.a: Confirm the running service uses the fixed build
options.b: Rely only on the commit message
options.c: Repeat the authorized test that reproduced the vulnerability

questions.explanation: Deployment verification and a targeted reproduction together test the fix on the running service.
